newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS sees mark gaining on Sfr on EMU deal.
newsitem.headline: CS sees mark gaining on Sfr on EMU deal.

text.p: CS Research said it expected the mark to gain against the Swiss franc on the strength of the European Union's agreement on a stability pact for members of the euro currency.

"On Friday mark/Swiss finished its consolidation. Today it will move up to 85.65 (Swiss centimes). The mark/Swiss will benefit from a higher dollar and lower mark crosses, creating the best international environment," it said in a forex comment.
"Furthermore, Swiss National Bank easing will support Swiss franc weakness," it said, adding short-term Swiss interest rates were "just collapsing" at the end of the reserve period.
"Dollar fundamentals look extremely healthy," it said, expecting the dollar to test successfully its recent high at 1.3360 francs later today.
In general, the EU's stability pact will weaken mark crosses for several reasons, it suggested.
"One, the stability pact exponentially increases the likelihood for EMU. This is a mark negative," it said.
"Two, the Bundesbank will have to ease its monetary policy massively. European bond and money futures markets will soar on that, creating the best environment for convergence trades."
It said countries like Italy, with its large, short-term financed public debt, would benefit more from that easing than Germany will.
Three, the deal eases pressure on the German government to paint a rosy picture of the economic outlook.

"Now, with the stability pact passed, the truth may come out. Thus expect a lot of negative news out of Germany as well as much hectic policy action. In our view, mark crosses are set for almost a free fall," it said.
It said the mark would test recent lows against the lira of 977 and then more important support at 968.
